record.original_question: Is the problem of computing directed pathwidth fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the width? Equivalently, although an XP algorithm is known for directed pathwidth on general digraphs, does there exist an FPT algorithm for this parameterized problem?

evidence.quote: There exists an XP algorithm to compute the directed pathwidth for the digraphs in general. It is open to know if an FPT algorithm exists or not (but probably not).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph. A directed path-decomposition of $D$ is a sequence $(X_1,X_2,\dots,X_r)$ of subsets of $V$ (called bags) such that:
(1) $\bigcup_{i=1}^{r} X_i = V$;
(2) for every vertex $v\in V$, the set of indices $\{i : v\in X_i\}$ forms a contiguous interval $[a_v,b_v]\subseteq\{1,\dots,r\}$;
(3) for every arc $(u,v)\in A$, there exist indices $i\le j$ with $u\in X_i$ and $v\in X_j$ (equivalently, $a_u\le b_v$).
The width of such a decomposition is $\max_{1\le i\le r}|X_i|-1$, and the directed pathwidth of $D$, denoted $\mathrm{dpw}(D)$, is the minimum width over all directed path-decompositions of $D$.

It is known that, for every fixed integer $k$, deciding whether $\mathrm{dpw}(D)\le k$ can be solved in time $n^{O(k)}$ on an $n$-vertex digraph (an XP algorithm).

Question: Does there exist a fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithm for computing the directed pathwidth parameterized by the width? Equivalently, is there a computable function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and a constant $c$ such that, given a digraph $D$ on $n$ vertices and a positive integer $k$, one can decide whether $\mathrm{dpw}(D)\le k$ in time $f(k)\cdot n^{c}$?
artifact.category_tag: parameterized complexity of digraph width measures
artifact.status_search_result: The fixed-parameter tractability of directed pathwidth on general digraphs (parameterized by the width $k$) appears to remain open. XP algorithms running in $n^{O(k)}$ are known, and FPT results exist only for special classes (e.g., semi-complete digraphs/tournaments via FPT-approximation, or under alternative parameterizations such as vertex cover number), but no FPT algorithm for general digraphs has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Pathwidth - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Undirected pathwidth is FPT (linear-time test for pathwidth ≤ k for any fixed k), in contrast to the directed case where the FPT status is unclear.
status_evidence.claim: Undirected pathwidth is FPT, while the directed case is not known to be FPT.

status_evidence.title: Computing the pathwidth of directed graphs with small vertex cover
status_evidence.snippet: FPT algorithm for directed pathwidth parameterized by vertex cover number.
status_evidence.claim: Directed pathwidth is FPT under alternative parameterizations, suggesting the natural parameterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: FPT-approximation for FPT Problems
status_evidence.snippet: FPT-approximation for pathwidth on tournaments and semi-complete digraphs.
status_evidence.claim: FPT (approximation) results known only for restricted digraph classes.
